changelog.name: Privacy Kit 3.7.1
changelog.body:
- Fix: some apps (e.g. Uber) could crash on launch with Boot ID spoofing enabled. Boot ID now disables itself automatically for any app it crashes, and is off by default for affected apps (Uber family).

Re-toggle Privacy Kit in LSPosed after updating.

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 3.7
changelog.body:
**Privacy Kit 3.7**

- Block hardware fingerprinting — a new per-app toggle that strips hardware-identifying media codecs and normalises CPU core count and GLES version, so fingerprinting SDKs can't re-identify the physical device
- Instant Update — apply hook, value and custom-hook changes live, without force-stopping the app
- Advertising ID and Firebase ID now update live when you change them
- New "Pause all spoofing" master switch (Developer options)
- Setup Doctor now checks the framework host and running targets, and can self-heal a missing scope
- Prove It shows the framework's live view of each app — whether the module is loaded and running right now, and warns if it failed to load
- Widevine DRM coherence in Balanced/Stealth (provisioningUniqueId is now per-profile) — pair with the v1.34 Zygisk companion
- Smoother scrolling and navigation; less typing lag in Custom Hooks
- Coherence fixes and repair of stale device identities
- Stability and crash fixes

Install: update in LSPosed, then flash/attach the Zygisk companion (privacykit-zygisk-v1.34.zip) and KPM module (privacykit_kpm.kpm). PrivacyKit-Probe is the optional identifier cross-check tool.

---

**If an app isn't being spoofed (quick checks):**
- Remove the app from the Magisk **Zygisk DenyList**, or turn **"Umount modules" off** on KSUN / SukiSU (or a custom app profile with it disabled).
- **Balanced / Stealth / Ultra:** keep the app **out** of LSPosed scope, but add **"Android System Framework"** + **Phone** (`com.android.phone`) to the scope and **reboot**.
- **KPM** is only needed for **Stealth & Ultra** (Standard/Balanced don't need it).
- **After updating:** re-toggle Privacy Kit in LSPosed and **force-stop** the app (or reboot).

Full setup & troubleshooting is in the module description (Troubleshooting section).

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 3.6
changelog.body:
**Privacy Kit 3.6**

- Isolated Play Services per profile — run a profile against its own anonymous Google Play Services (a fresh checkin / device ID, a new advertising ID and no Google account) so it looks like a different device to Google
- The real Google account is now hidden in every spoof mode when a profile's Play Services are isolated
- Boot ID is now a per-profile identifier (Device Identifiers) — leave it real, pin a stable one, or set your own
- Fake Google account per profile (a chosen or generated Gmail)
- Per-profile isolation of Chromium browser data (Local Storage, cookies)
- Coherence fixes for locale, date/timezone, SIM and system properties
- Stability and crash fixes across the app

Install: update in LSPosed, then flash/attach the Zygisk companion (privacykit-zygisk-v1.33.zip) and KPM module (privacykit_kpm.kpm). PrivacyKit-Probe is the optional identifier cross-check tool.

---

**If an app isn't being spoofed (quick checks):**
- Remove the app from the Magisk **Zygisk DenyList**, or turn **"Umount modules" off** on KSUN / SukiSU (or a custom app profile with it disabled).
- **Balanced / Stealth / Ultra:** keep the app **out** of LSPosed scope, but add **"Android System Framework"** + **Phone** (`com.android.phone`) to the scope and **reboot**.
- **KPM** is only needed for **Stealth & Ultra** (Standard/Balanced don't need it).
- **After updating:** re-toggle Privacy Kit in LSPosed and **force-stop** the app (or reboot).

Full setup & troubleshooting is in the module description (Troubleshooting section).

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 3.5.1
changelog.body:
Privacy Kit 3.5.1

- Minor fix to a bundled dashboard script that could fail to load

Install the APK through LSPosed and reboot. Optional companions attached: Zygisk module, kernel module (KPM), keystore-isolation module, and PK Probe.

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 3.5
changelog.body:
Privacy Kit 3.5

- Each profile now presents a distinct device on phones newer than the built-in device catalog — profiles no longer share one identity
- Per-app display refresh rate and supported-modes spoofing, matched to the spoofed device
- Widevine DRM level and system ID spoofing, kept consistent with the device
- Phantom SIM: report a SIM present and coherent with the spoofed carrier
- Proxy egress through the kernel with no VPN prompt on supported setups, with VPN fallback
- Proxy location identity re-aligns automatically when a profile's proxy changes
- Share a device identity as a short code to copy and paste between profiles
- Advertising ID now stays consistent across apps in the same profile

Install the APK through LSPosed and reboot. Optional companions attached: Zygisk module, kernel module (KPM), keystore-isolation module, and PK Probe.

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 3.4
changelog.body:
Privacy Kit 3.4

- Isolating an app for the first time now keeps its existing data as a separate "Original" profile instead of clearing it
- Locale and timezone spoofing now apply in every spoof mode
- Setup Doctor: one "Check coherence & diagnose" action with a one-tap Fix
- Self-service diagnostics — export a report, diagnose with AI, or send it to the developer
- Device-info divergence reduced to zero across all spoof modes
- boot_id spoofing through the kernel module
- Fixed a kernel version identifier leak
- Community configs: local import and AI generate
- Launch stability and cross-layer coherence fixes

Install the APK through LSPosed and reboot. Optional companions attached: Zygisk module, kernel module (KPM), keystore-isolation module, and PK Probe.

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 3.2
changelog.body:
- Community Addons: browse, import and share configs, hooks and app scripts.
- App Scripts: shell / HTML / Lua automation with scheduling and a custom-script loader.
- Per-app Spoof Modes — Standard, Balanced, Stealth, Ultra — with auto-escalation.
- Per-profile proxy pools, bulk proxy import, and auto region-match to your proxy's country.
- Carrier-coherent SIM per country and per-profile kernel (KPM) identity.
- Automatic keystore isolation for Meta apps and WhatsApp.
- Donor-dump export to clone an identity across profiles or devices.
- Stronger identity coherence and stealth, plus proxy and stability fixes.

Install PrivacyKit-3.2.apk, reboot, enable in LSPosed. Optional: zygisk-v1.22 (native), kpm (APatch), Keystore-Isolation (stealth keystore), Probe (self-test).

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 2.3.1
changelog.body:
This repo release brings the 2.3 feature wave and the 2.3.1 anti-fingerprint hardening (the previous repo release was 2.2).

## 2.3.1 — anti-fingerprint hardening
Closes the remaining VD Infos spoof-detector divergences seen on a spoofed dual-SIM profile:
- IMEI coherence: radio/RIL properties (persist.radio.imei*, ro.ril.oem.imei*, ro.ril.miui.imei*, ril.imei*, gsm.device.imei*, persist.sys.imei*) now return the profile's spoofed IMEI on every lens (Java, native, shell), not the real radio IMEI.
- Owner name: persist.sys.device_name is spoofed to the profile hostname.
- bluetooth_name: the settings-provider bulk query and GET_secure call now return the spoofed name (previously only Settings.Secure.getString was covered).
- ADB / developer options: Settings.System.getInt is hooked, so a cross-store getInt sweep no longer disagrees.
- Hide VPN: tun/tap/ppp/ipsec/wg interfaces are hidden from a `ls /sys/class/net` listing on the Java NetworkInterface, Runtime.exec and native popen lenses.
- Ships native companion v1.17.

## 2.3 — App Scripts, proxy coherence, Pro-by-email
- App Scripts: per-app root shell scripting with parameters, scheduling, live streaming output, custom HTML UIs and an AI bridge.
- Network: connecting a per-app proxy auto-matches locale, timezone, SIM/carrier, country and GPS to the proxy's exit country; a proxied app re-activates its proxy automatically on open.
- Location: an AI assistant turns a plain-language goal into a geocoded, road-snapped, time-paced route.
- Pro: activate with your email alongside your key.

## Assets
- **PrivacyKit-2.3.1.apk** — the LSPosed module. Install, reboot, then enable it in LSPosed and add your apps.
- **privacykit-zygisk-v1.17.zip** — optional native companion (Magisk / KernelSU module: flash and reboot) that closes the native and shell spoofing lenses.
- **PrivacyKit-Probe-2.3.1.apk** — optional self-test app that reports which lenses are covered.
- **privacykit_kpm.kpm** — optional APatch KPM (Tier-2 framework mode, off by default).

changelog.name: Privacy Kit 2.2
changelog.body:
Privacy Kit 2.2

Anti-fingerprint & coherence
* Close the remaining VD-Infos divergences: Settings-provider values and MEID
* Emit the build date natively (ro.build.date), anchored to the fingerprint's build-ID date
* Pair the in-process native property lens with the shell getprop spoof; pre-touch COW props so more props patch in place
* Coherent package hide-list across every enumeration lens — Java, native and shell package counts now match
* Close the SUPPORTED_ABIS and /proc/meminfo lens splits
* Device-real profiles: fix Build field/prop, kernel and locale coherence
* Pin the native property exporter's resolve() to the fingerprint, matching the Xposed hook
* Ship native companion v1.14

Location
* Map-first editor — pick a point on a map instead of typing coordinates
* Live drive view with a moving position, progress and a stop control
* Follow real roads via snap-to-roads, with a straight-line fallback when offline
* Draw a route by hand; open the map at your current location; fix tapping a saved favourite

Network
* Honest local proxy tunnel — the notification and UI now explain the one-time VPN prompt and that the only exit is your proxy
* Fix a proxy-egress teardown that could leak the real IP

Interface
* Merge the four diagnostics screens into a single Verify screen
* Render Markdown (bold, italic, code and code blocks) in the AI assistant chat
* Setup Doctor recognises the COW property engine as active native hooking

Fixes
* Stop hiding Privacy Kit from getPackageInfo, so LSPosed can detect module updates
* Container-restore hardening

readme:
![Privacy Kit banner](assets/privacy-kit-banner.png)

# Privacy Kit

Privacy Kit is an LSPosed module for Android. It gives each app you pick its own
fake device identity, instead of changing identifiers for the whole phone. Apps
that read stable device IDs see a made-up device, not your real one.

It does not make you anonymous. Apps can still track you by login, IP address,
network metadata, browser state and server-side checks. Privacy Kit only covers
on-device identifiers.

Package: `com.sal.privacykit`. Current version: `3.6` (versionCode 110).

## What a release contains

Only the app APK is required. The rest are optional layers that reach deeper
below the app.

| File | What it is | Needs |
|---|---|---|
| `PrivacyKit-<ver>.apk` | The app and LSPosed module. Spoofs Java-layer IDs per selected app. | LSPosed |
| `privacykit-zygisk-<ver>.zip` | Native companion. Covers system properties, `/proc`, `/sys`, Wi-Fi MAC and the kernel string. | Magisk, KernelSU or APatch (Zygisk) |
| `privacykit_kpm.kpm` | Kernel module, advanced. File timestamps, `/proc/cpuinfo`, CPU frequencies. | APatch with KPM |
| `PrivacyKit-Probe-<ver>.apk` | Self-test app. Shows which IDs are actually spoofed and which still leak. | none |

## Features

- Per-app profiles for the apps you choose.
- Spoofs Android ID, GSF ID, Advertising ID, App Set ID, Widevine/DRM ID, serial,
  build properties, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth values, hostname, IMEI, MEID, IMSI, ICCID
  and phone number.
- Per-identifier rules: real value, fixed value, random per launch, random daily,
  or your own value.
- Device templates for common phones, or build your own.
- Optional root-based data isolation between profiles.
- Optional per-profile SOCKS5 proxy (Pro).
- Backup and restore, import and export, launch history, and a built-in verify screen.

## Requirements

- Android 8.0 or newer.
- LSPosed, on Magisk, KernelSU or APatch.
- Root is optional. It is only needed for data isolation and the native and kernel layers.

## Install

1. Download the APK from Releases and install it.
2. Open Privacy Kit once so LSPosed can detect it.
3. Enable the module in LSPosed and tick the apps you want in scope.
4. Reboot, or force-stop the target apps.
5. In Privacy Kit, add an app, create a profile, and launch it.

For the native layer, flash `privacykit-zygisk-<ver>.zip` in your root manager and reboot.

## Spoof modes

Every app you add has a spoof mode. The mode decides which layers do the spoofing,
from the widest and most detectable to the quietest. Standard is the default. Move
an app to a quieter mode only if it notices the hooks or crashes.

There are five layers underneath, from the widest and most detectable (T1) to the
quietest (T5):

| Tier | Layer | Where it runs | What it spoofs | Detectability | Needs |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | LSPosed Java hooks | Inside the app process (Xposed) | The widest set of Java-layer identifiers | Highest — easiest for an app to detect | App ticked in LSPosed scope |
| **T2** | Zygisk native inline hooks | Inside the app process (native) | GL strings and some system properties | Medium — a few hardened apps crash on this layer | Zygisk (Magisk / KernelSU / APatch) |
| **T3** | Zygisk native JNI | Inside the app process (native, no trampolines) | `Build.*` fields and system properties | Low — no inline trampolines, survives most anti-hook checks | Zygisk |
| **T4** | Framework | `system_server` — nothing is added to the app | Android ID, serial and telephony IDs | Very low — nothing is injected into the app | Built in (no extra module) |
| **T5** | KPM (kernel module) | The kernel, below libc and below the app | cpuinfo, CPU frequencies, `if_inet6`, install dates, Wi-Fi MAC, and Android ID / advertising ID | Lowest — runs beneath the app entirely | APatch with KPM (see below) |

| Mode | Layers | In LSPosed scope | Covers | Reads real |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Standard | T1 + T2 + T3 | yes | everything Privacy Kit can spoof | nothing extra |
| Balanced | T2 + T3 + T4 | no, remove it | Build, properties and IDs, no Xposed in the process | nothing extra |
| Stealth | T3 + T4 + T5 | no, remove it | Build and properties via JNI, IDs, kernel files, no inline hooks | nothing extra |
| Ultra | T4 + T5 | no, remove it | Android ID and IDs at the source, plus kernel files, nothing in the app | Build, model and properties |

Set the mode on each app's Spoof Mode screen. Balanced, Stealth and Ultra want the
app out of the LSPosed scope; Privacy Kit makes its own Java hooks inert for that
app and reminds you. Stealth and Ultra use the kernel module, so they need APatch.
Ultra is the quietest, but since nothing runs in the app it shows the real model
and build, so a check that compares your Android ID against your model can still
notice. Stealth adds the native layer back for a coherent device without inline
hooks.

## KPM guide (APatch kernel module)

The KPM is the T5 kernel layer. It runs below libc and below the app, so an app's
anti-hook checks find nothing in its own process. It is optional, and only the
Stealth and Ultra modes use it.

You need:

- APatch with KernelPatch (KPM) support. Magisk, KernelSU and SukiSU cannot run a
  KPM. The KPM controls still appear on those, but the kernel tier is marked
  unavailable and turning it on just does nothing.
- The module file `privacykit_kpm.kpm`. It ships next to the release, not inside
  the APK. It is built against a kernel, so you may have to build it for yours. The
  module source is in `zygisk-privacykit/kpm/` in the Privacy_Kit repo.
- Your APatch superkey.
- A way back in, such as fastboot or a custom recovery. A bad kernel module can
  stop the phone from booting.

Set it up:

1. Push the module once with `adb push privacykit_kpm.kpm /data/local/tmp/privacykit_kpm.kpm`. Any root file copy works too.
2. Open Privacy Kit, then Settings, Developer, the KPM section. Paste your APatch
   superkey and tap Save superkey. It is checked once, stored encrypted, never
   shown again, and left out of backups.
3. Set the apps you want to Stealth or Ultra, or turn on Kernel module (KPM) in
   Developer settings. Privacy Kit loads the module through APatch
   (`kpatch <superkey> kpm load`). Setup Doctor has a one-tap Load if it is not up.
4. The module does not stay loaded across a reboot on its own. Privacy Kit reloads
   it on boot when you have KPM apps and a saved superkey. If it is ever down,
   Setup Doctor shows it and offers Load.

What it spoofs:

- Files: `/proc/cpuinfo`, `/proc/version`, `/proc/net/if_inet6`, CPU frequencies,
  the Wi-Fi MAC at `/sys/class/net/wlan0/address`, and the app install date.
- IDs, per app: Android ID, advertising ID and the Widevine device ID, rewritten
  in the kernel. This reaches the normal read path; the cursor query path stays
  real. It needs a current module (1.6.0) and only runs once Privacy Kit arms it,
  so an older loaded KPM may leave these IDs real.
- Everything is per app and only for normal apps. Root and system still read the
  real device.

What it does not do:

- It does not touch `Build.*` or system properties. Those come from the native or
  framework layers, so Ultra on its own shows the real model and build. Use Stealth
  if you want those spoofed too.
- It does not defeat hardware keystore or Play Integrity attestation.
- It does not spoof IMEI, serial, IMSI, ICCID or Bluetooth. A normal app cannot
  read those anyway.
- The cpuinfo, frequency and version text is filled in by your AI provider if you
  set one. Without it, the install date, `if_inet6` and Wi-Fi MAC are still
  spoofed, and the rest is skipped rather than faked badly.

## Troubleshooting

**App is not being spoofed — check root hiding first.** Privacy Kit works through
Zygisk and mounts, so if your root manager *hides modules* from the target app, that
app sees the real, un-spoofed device.

- Magisk: remove the app from the **Zygisk DenyList** (or keep DenyList off).
- KernelSU-Next (KSUN) / SukiSU-Ultra: turn **"Umount modules" off**, or give the app
  a **custom app profile with Umount modules disabled**.

**Balanced, Stealth or Ultra — set the LSPosed scope correctly.** These modes want the
target app **out** of the LSPosed scope (Privacy Kit uses the native and framework
layers instead and makes its own Java hooks inert for that app — it reminds you). But
the Framework layer that serves Android ID, serial and telephony runs in
`system_server`, so Privacy Kit also needs **"Android System Framework"** (system_server)
and the **Phone** app (`com.android.phone`) ticked in its LSPosed scope — add them and
**reboot**. If Android ID, serial or SIM/telephony IDs read real in Balanced or Stealth,
this is almost always why.

**KPM is optional.** Only the **Stealth and Ultra** modes use the kernel module.
**Standard and Balanced do not need it** — skip the `.kpm` unless you want those modes
(see the KPM guide above).

**After updating Privacy Kit.** **Re-toggle** the module in LSPosed (turn it off, then
on) and **force-stop** the target app so the new code loads. If you have no LSPosed
Manager installed, **reboot** instead.

**Other common fixes.**

- Turn on **Native Spoofing (Zygisk)** in Developer settings — Balanced and Stealth need it.
- Open apps with **"Launch with this profile"** inside Privacy Kit, not the normal app
  icon, so the isolated profile actually mounts.
- After changing a mode, profile or identifier, **force-stop and relaunch** the app.
- Run **Setup Doctor** (Settings) — it checks LSPosed, scope, the native module, KPM,
  battery and notifications in one tap.
- Exempt Privacy Kit from **battery optimization** so background re-mounts survive.
- App will not launch, or shows another profile's data: use **Fix stuck mounts**
  (Developer settings), then relaunch.
- Leave **Boot ID** on Real unless you need it — a spoofed boot_id crashes some apps.

## Source

Source code, build instructions and the licensing server:
https://github.com/Mohithash/privacy-kit-lite

## Build your own ROM with it

Besides this LSPosed module, the same per-app spoofing runs inside the Android
framework, with no injection, in BestROM, an open-source AOSP 17 ROM (first device
POCO F6 / peridot). Nothing is injected into the app process, so this is the
cleanest mode. You can build your own ROM with Privacy Kit baked in; the source
tree ships an MCP server so a coding agent can sync, build and verify it.

- BestROM: https://github.com/Mohithash/bestrom-project
- Build (manifest): https://github.com/Mohithash/manifest

## A note from me

I am an independent developer from India, and I work on this alone. I want to be
honest about why you will see a paid Pro tier and a donate option here.

The last while has been hard. I lost my job, I was cheated out of money, and I am
dealing with a legal case, all while supporting my wife and our home. I still like
building this and I want to keep it going.

If Privacy Kit is useful to you, buying Pro or sending a small donation genuinely
helps me and my family. It is never required, and the free features stay free. If
you would rather help with code, testing or ideas, that is very welcome too.

I made this private project public to get through a hard time. Once it reaches my goal of about $5,000 in total earnings I plan to open-source it, so buying Pro or donating now both helps my family and brings that closer.

Thank you for trying it.

## Support and contact

- Pro, donations or questions: Telegram @couponxdealer (message me for UPI or other options).
- Updates: Telegram @privacykit.

Please do not send money to anyone who is not listed here.

## License

No open-source license is set. All rights reserved by the author. If you want to
reuse, redistribute or modify it publicly, please ask first.

## Disclaimer

Use Privacy Kit only on devices and accounts you are allowed to modify. It is for
privacy, testing and personal device control. I am not responsible for account
bans, data loss, device problems, or any app's terms being broken.

# 隐私套件

Privacy Kit 是 Android 的 LSPod 模块。它为您选择的每个应用程序提供了自己的
伪造设备身份，而不是更改整个手机的标识符。应用程序
读取稳定设备 ID 的人看到的是虚构的设备，而不是真实的设备。

它不会让您匿名。应用程序仍然可以通过登录名、IP 地址来跟踪您，
网络元数据、浏览器状态和服务器端检查。隐私套件仅涵盖
设备上的标识符。

包：`com.sal.privacykit`。当前版本：“3.6”（版本代码 110）。

## 发行版包含哪些内容

仅需要应用程序 APK。其余的都是可选层，可以达到更深层次
在应用程序下方。

|文件 |它是什么 |需求|
|---|---|---|
| `PrivacyKit-<ver>.apk` |应用程序和 LSPoded 模块。欺骗每个选定应用程序的 Java 层 ID。 | LS 构成 |
| `privacykit-zygisk-<版本>.zip` |原生伴侣。涵盖系统属性、`/proc`、`/sys`、Wi-Fi MAC 和内核字符串。 | Magisk、KernelSU 或 APatch (Zygisk) |
| `privacykit_kpm.kpm` |内核模块，高级。文件时间戳、`/proc/cpuinfo`、CPU 频率。 |与 KPM 的 APatch |
| `PrivacyKit-Probe-<ver>.apk` |自测试应用程序。显示哪些 ID 确实被欺骗，哪些 ID 仍然泄漏。 |无 |

## 特点

- 您选择的应用程序的每个应用程序配置文件。
- 欺骗 Android ID、GSF ID、广告 ID、应用程序集 ID、Widevine/DRM ID、序列号、
  构建属性、Wi-Fi 和蓝牙值、主机名、IMEI、MEID、IMSI、ICCID
  和电话号码。
- 每个标识符规则：实际值、固定值、每次启动随机、每日随机、
  或者你自己的价值。
- 适用于常见手机的设备模板，或构建您自己的设备模板。
- 配置文件之间可选的基于根的数据隔离。
- 可选的每个配置文件 SOCKS5 代理（专业版）。
- 备份和恢复、导入和导出、启动历史记录以及内置验证屏幕。

## 要求

- Android 8.0 或更高版本。
- LSPod，在 Magisk、KernelSU 或 APatch 上。
- 根是可选的。仅数据隔离以及本机层和内核层需要它。

## 安装

1. 从 Releases 下载 APK 并安装。
2. 打开一次 Privacy Kit，以便 LSPod 可以检测到它。
3. 在 LSPod 中启用该模块并勾选您想要在范围内的应用程序。
4. 重新启动或强制停止目标应用程序。
5. 在 Privacy Kit 中，添加应用程序、创建配置文件并启动它。

对于本机层，在根管理器中刷新“privacykit-zygisk-<ver>.zip”并重新启动。

## 恶搞模式

您添加的每个应用程序都有欺骗模式。该模式决定哪些层进行欺骗，
从最宽、最容易察觉到最安静。标准是默认值。移动
仅当应用程序注意到挂钩或崩溃时才会进入更安静的模式。

下面有五层，从最宽和最容易检测到的 (T1) 到
最安静（T5）：

|等级 |层 |它在哪里运行 |它欺骗了什么 |可检测性|需求|
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **T1** | LSPod Java 钩子 |应用程序进程内部（Xposed）|最广泛的 Java 层标识符集 |最高 - 最容易被应用程序检测到 |应用程序在 LSPoded 范围内打勾 |
| **T2** | Zygisk 原生内联钩子 |应用程序进程内部（本机）| GL 字符串和一些系统属性 |中 - 一些强化的应用程序在这一层崩溃 | Zygisk（Magisk / KernelSU / APatch）|
| **T3** | Zygisk 原生 JNI |应用程序进程内部（本机，无蹦床）| `Build.*` 字段和系统属性 |低 — 无内联蹦床，可通过大多数防钩检查 |齐吉斯克 |
| **T4** |框架| `system_server` — 应用程序中没有添加任何内容 | Android ID、序列号和电话 ID |非常低——没有任何东西被注入到应用程序中|内置（无额外模块）|
| **T5** | KPM（内核模块）|内核，libc 下面和应用程序下面 | cpuinfo、CPU 频率、`if_inet6`、安装日期、Wi-Fi MAC 和 Android ID/广告 ID |最低 — 完全在应用程序下方运行 |带有 KPM 的 APatch（见下文）|

|模式|层 |在 LSPod 范围内 |封面|读真实|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|标准|T1 + T2 + T3 |是的 |隐私套件可以欺骗一切|没什么额外的|
|平衡 | T2 + T3 + T4 |不，删除它 |构建、属性和 ID，进程中没有 Xpose |没什么额外的|
|隐身| T3 + T4 + T5 |不，删除它 |通过 JNI、ID、内核文件构建和属性，无内联挂钩 |没什么额外的|
|超| T4 + T5 |不，删除它 | Android ID 和源代码中的 ID，加上内核文件，应用程序中没有任何内容 |构建、模型和属性 |

在每个应用程序的欺骗模式屏幕上设置模式。平衡、隐形和超想要
应用程序超出 LSPod 范围； Privacy Kit 使其自己的 Java 钩子对此保持惰性
应用程序并提醒您。 Stealth和Ultra使用内核模块，因此需要APatch。
Ultra 是最安静的，但由于应用程序中没有任何运行，因此它显示的是真实模型
并构建，因此将您的 Android ID 与您的型号进行比较的检查仍然可以
注意。 Stealth 为无需内联的连贯设备添加了本机层
钩子。

## KPM指南（APatch内核模块）

KPM 是T5 内核层。它在 libc 和应用程序下方运行，因此应用程序的
反挂钩检查在其自身进程中找不到任何内容。它是可选的，并且只有
隐形和超级模式使用它。

您需要：

- 具有 KernelPatch (KPM) 支持的 APatch。 Magisk、KernelSU 和 SukiSU 无法运行
  关键绩效管理。 KPM 控件仍然出现在这些控件上，但内核层已标记
  不可用并且打开它什么也不做。
- 模块文件`privacykit_kpm.kpm`。它在版本旁边发布，而不是在版本内发布
  该APK。它是针对内核构建的，因此您可能必须为您的内核构建它。的
  模块源位于 Privacy_Kit 存储库中的“zygisk-privacykit/kpm/”中。
- 您的 APatch 超级密钥。
- 一种返回方式，例如快速启动或自定义恢复。错误的内核模块可能会
  阻止手机启动。

设置它：

1. 使用 `adb push Privacykit_kpm.kpm /data/local/tmp/privacykit_kpm.kpm` 推送模块一次。任何根文件副本也可以。
2. 打开 Privacy Kit，然后打开“设置”、“开发人员”、“KPM”部分。粘贴你的APatch
   超级密钥并点击保存超级密钥。它被检查一次，加密存储，永远不会
   再次显示，并省略备份。
3. 将您想要的应用程序设置为 Stealth 或 Ultra，或在
   开发者设置。 Privacy Kit通过APatch加载模块
   （`kpatch <superkey> kpm load`）。如果未启动，Setup Doctor 具有一键加载功能。
4. 模块在重新启动后不会自行保持加载状态。隐私套件重新加载
   当您拥有 KPM 应用程序和已保存的超级密钥时，它会在启动时启动。如果一直跌下去的话
   安装医生显示它并提供加载。

它欺骗了什么：

- 文件：`/proc/cpuinfo`、`/proc/version`、`/proc/net/if_inet6`、CPU 频率、
  Wi-Fi MAC（位于“/sys/class/net/wlan0/address”）以及应用程序安装日期。
- 每个应用程序的 ID：Android ID、广告 ID 和 Widevine 设备 ID，已重写
  在内核中。这样就到达了正常的读取路径；光标查询路径保持不变
  真实的。它需要一个当前模块（1.6.0）并且仅在隐私套件装备它后运行，
  因此较旧加载的 KPM 可能会保留这些 ID 为真实值。
- 一切都是针对每个应用程序的，并且仅适用于普通应用程序。 root 和系统仍然读取
  真实设备。

它不做什么：

- 它不会触及“Build.*”或系统属性。那些来自本地或
  框架层，因此 Ultra 本身显示了真实的模型和构建。使用隐身
  如果你也想要那些被欺骗的。
- 它不会破坏硬件密钥库或 Play 完整性证明。
- 它不会欺骗 IMEI、序列号、IMSI、ICCID 或蓝牙。普通应用程序无法
  无论如何，请阅读这些内容。
- cpuinfo、频率和版本文本由您的 AI 提供商填写，如果您
  设置一个。如果没有它，安装日期、“if_inet6”和 Wi-Fi MAC 仍然是
  欺骗，其余的被跳过而不是严重伪造。

## 故障排除

**应用程序没有被欺骗 - 首先检查根隐藏。**隐私套件通过
Zygisk 和挂载，因此如果您的根管理器*从目标应用程序中隐藏模块*，那么
应用程序看到真实的、未被欺骗的设备。

- Magisk：从 **Zygisk DenyList** 中删除应用程序（或保持 DenyList 关闭）。
- KernelSU-Next (KSUN) / SukiSU-Ultra：关闭 **“卸载模块”**，或给予应用程序
  **禁用卸载模块的自定义应用程序配置文件**。

**平衡、隐形或超 — 正确设置 LSPod 范围。** 这些模式需要
目标应用程序 **超出** LSPod 范围（Privacy Kit 使用本机和框架
而是分层并使其自己的 Java 钩子对该应用程序无效 - 它提醒您）。但是
提供 Android ID、串行和电话服务的框架层运行在
`system_server`，因此Privacy Kit还需要**“Android系统框架”**（system_server）
并且 **Phone** 应用程序 (`com.android.phone`) 在其 LSPod 范围内打勾 - 添加它们并
**重新启动**。如果 Android ID、序列号或 SIM/电话 ID 在 Balanced 或 Stealth 中读取为真实值，
这几乎总是原因。

**KPM 是可选的。** 只有 **Stealth 和 Ultra** 模式使用内核模块。
**标准和平衡不需要它** — 跳过 `.kpm` 除非您想要这些模式
（请参阅上面的 KPM 指南）。

**更新隐私套件后。** **重新切换** LSPosed 中的模块（将其关闭，然后
on）并**强制停止**目标应用程序，以便加载新代码。如果你没有 LSPosed
已安装管理器，**重新启动**。

**其他常见修复。**

- 在开发者设置中打开 **本机欺骗 (Zygisk)** - 平衡和隐形需要它。
- 在隐私套件中使用**“使用此配置文件启动”**打开应用程序，而不是普通应用程序
  图标，因此隔离的配置文件实际上已安装。
- 更改模式、配置文件或标识符后，**强制停止并重新启动**应用程序。
- 运行 **Setup Doctor**（设置）——它检查 LSPod、范围、本机模块、KPM、
  一键查看电池和通知。
- 使隐私套件免受**电池优化**的影响，这样后台重新安装就可以生存。
- 应用程序将无法启动，或显示另一个配置文件的数据：使用**修复卡住的安装**
  （开发者设置），然后重新启动。
- 除非您需要，否则将 **Boot ID** 保留为 Real - 欺骗性的 boot_id 会导致某些应用程序崩溃。
